findings.title: PrimaryWidget's library-operation guard has no automated test, and the mutation-test gap it represents has been named on every loop of this project's history
findings.why_it_matters: isLibraryOperationRunning's try-begin/end rule is the single mechanism preventing a bulk library reload and a single-game write (or two single-game writes) from racing each other; F-014 proved the rule's coverage was once incomplete, and nothing in this repository can mechanically re-prove it stays complete. test_strategy has scored exactly 6.5 SAME on all 13 loops of this project's recorded history citing this exact gap, and architecture_quality has been flat at 7.5 for 9 of those.
findings.what_is_wrong: IsLibraryOperationBlocking/TryBeginLibraryOperation/EndLibraryOperation (pre-fix PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:194-232) implement the mutual-exclusion rule directly against a private bool isLibraryOperationRunning field, inline in a WinUI Page class. Per TESTING.md, PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs binds to Windows.UI.Xaml, which has no desktop projection in this repo's xunit infrastructure - so this rule could never be tested in place, unlike every other compute concern in this codebase (GameImages, OperationReport, ManifestEntryIdentity), which TESTING.md documents as already extracted and covered for exactly this reason.
findings.leverage_impact: Before the fix, no caller - human reviewer or future refactor - could get a machine-checked guarantee that the mutual-exclusion rule still holds; confidence depended entirely on reading three methods together and trusting they agree, the same failure mode named at F-001/F-005 through F-009/F-014.
findings.locality_impact: Contained: the rule's decision logic moves to one 20-line class with no dependents beyond PrimaryWidget; the rule's UI side effects stay in PrimaryWidget, matching the split TESTING.md already uses.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Not a live bug (F-014's fix independently re-confirmed holding), but the single highest-value untested surface in the codebase by the severity anchor's own language, and the only scorecard gap that survived unchanged through all 13 of this project's loops without an actionable, unblocked fix.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extract the guard's begin/end/is-running state machine into a new internal sealed class LibraryOperationGuard in Services/Library/ (no WinUI dependency), and have PrimaryWidget's three wrapper methods delegate to it while keeping their own UI side effects unchanged. Add LibraryOperationGuardTests.cs asserting the exact mutation named above. No new Seam - a plain class, directly testable, following the OperationReport.cs precedent already established in this codebase.

findings.title: LoadGameEntriesAsync resolves each unmatched game's name and SteamGridDB match sequentially, one network round trip at a time, on every widget open
findings.why_it_matters: On a library with many unmatched games, the fully-sequential per-entry network chain adds latency that scales linearly with library size.
findings.what_is_wrong: LoadGameEntriesAsync's per-entry loop (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:455-717, pre-fix line numbers) awaits each entry's SteamGridDB platform-ID lookup, store name-fetch and SteamGridDB name search in strict sequence, even though the awaits are independent across entries.
findings.locality_impact: Would be contained to PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs if unblocked.
findings.why_weakens_submission: A real, linearly-scaling latency cost, but BLOCKED: the recorded standing user constraint (no behavioural oracle for per-game network-call ordering/concurrency changes against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft) means this loop cannot land a change altering observable call ordering/concurrency/count against those services without a product decision this loop cannot make. Re-derived fresh this loop: a pure extraction would not be blocked, but F-011's own remedy (bounded concurrency) necessarily changes network-call ordering, so it stays genuinely blocked.
findings.minimal_correction_path: BLOCKED this loop; named for continuity (Backlog Prioritization Pass criterion 0) rather than escalated to a user-decision halt, since F-016 filled this loop's actionable Priority-1 slot.

findings.title: SteamGridDbClient.NoteCapsuleParse and FixLog perform unsynchronized check-then-populate/append writes on static mutable collections, the same defect class F-015 just fixed in StoreNameLookup
findings.why_it_matters: Both are safe today only by the same single-threaded-per-load convention that made StoreNameLookup's three caches safe before F-015 fixed them last loop. Neither guarantee is enforced by the fields themselves - a future concurrent caller (including a future unblocked F-011) would silently inherit an unsynchronized write, exactly the risk F-015's own fix eliminated for StoreNameLookup.
findings.what_is_wrong: SteamGridDbClient.NoteCapsuleParse (SteamGridDbClient.cs:49-55) checks CapsuleParseNotes.Count < 5 then calls CapsuleParseNotes.Add(note) with no lock - a TOCTOU race on a List<string>, which is not thread-safe for concurrent Add calls even individually. FixLog's three static fields (lines/fileName/logFolder, FixLog.cs:24,26,28) are mutated by Start()/Write()/read by SaveAsync() with no synchronization at all.
findings.leverage_impact: A caller gets no concurrent-access-safety guarantee from either type's Interface alone; safety depends entirely on today's callers happening to be sequential.
findings.locality_impact: SteamGridDbClient.cs's fix is fully contained to that file; FixLog.cs's fix is fully contained to that file - two independent, small remedies, not one shared abstraction.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Not currently reachable as a live race (LoadGameEntriesAsync's loop awaits one entry at a time; FixLog's two callers are mutually exclusive under the library-operation guard), but the identical structural inconsistency F-015 closed in StoreNameLookup last loop, found in two more locations this loop.
findings.minimal_correction_path: SteamGridDbClient: wrap NoteCapsuleParse's check-then-populate body in a dedicated SemaphoreSlim gate, matching StoreNameLookup's per-cache gate pattern (F-015's own remedy). FixLog: same pattern, or fold the three fields into one small owned type analogous to OperationReport.

findings.title: GamePlatformHelper's Xbox-folder-name and SteamGridDB-API-string mappings are two independent switch statements over GamePlatform with no shared source of truth
findings.why_it_matters: Adding or renaming a platform requires remembering to update both switches; nothing fails to compile if one is forgotten (both silently default to Unknown/null).
findings.what_is_wrong: FromXboxDirectory (GamePlatform.cs:22-46) and GamePlatformToSGDBApiString (GamePlatform.cs:48-67) independently switch over the same platform cases with no shared table; FromXboxDirectory additionally handles legacy folder-name aliases with no analogue in the reverse mapping. Re-confirmed unchanged via direct full read this loop.
findings.leverage_impact: Each new platform pays this asserted-twice tax; small today, compounds at scale.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Minor, but the enum's own home module holds two independent interpretations of itself with no compiler-enforced link. This loop's Adversarial Pass re-tested the smallest fix and confirmed it still fails Simplify Pressure Test Q5 against F-016.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Fold both mappings into one table keyed by GamePlatform, with a separate small alias list for FromXboxDirectory's legacy folder names.

narrative: Place, not win, yet - but this loop breaks new ground rather than repeating the pattern of the last three. Concurrency is credited for a real, verified fix (F-015, landed loop 3) while this loop's own investigation immediately found the same defect class recurring in a second location (F-017, new, queued) - closing one instance of a defect class does not close the class. The larger event this loop is F-016: for the first time in this project's 13-loop history, the test_strategy gap that every prior loop named and declined to act on has an actionable, unblocked, low-risk fix, and this loop takes it - not by inventing new architecture, but by applying a pattern this codebase already uses everywhere else (TESTING.md's documented Compute/Do split). Runtime ownership remains trustworthy for every traced write path (F-014 holds, independently re-verified). Simplification did not hurt this loop: zero new ceremony, zero new Seams, a plain class following an established precedent. Tests newly cover a primary-flow concurrency-safety mechanism no test in this repository could previously reach at all. Future work still risks over-engineering if it tries to extract PrimaryWidget's orchestration wholesale, unify StoreNameLookup's differently-shaped caches, or extract the session-token pattern before a third instance justifies it; this loop re-examined all three candidates independently and reached the same restrained conclusions prior loops did.

loop_result.what_changed: Extracted PrimaryWidget's library-operation guard (isLibraryOperationRunning plus the begin/end/is-running rule in IsLibraryOperationBlocking/TryBeginLibraryOperation/EndLibraryOperation) into a new internal sealed class LibraryOperationGuard (SteamGridDB.Xbox/Services/Library/LibraryOperationGuard.cs) with a bool IsRunning, bool TryBegin() and void End() - no WinUI dependency. PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs's three wrapper methods now delegate their state-transition decision to a private readonly LibraryOperationGuard field while keeping their own UI side effects (StatusText.Text, SetHeaderButtonsEnabled) exactly where and when they ran before. Registered the new file in SteamGridDB.Xbox.csproj. Added SteamGridDB.Xbox.Tests/LibraryOperationGuardTests.cs with five tests.
loop_result.evidence_change_is_honest: Full build (msbuild SteamGridDB.Xbox.sln /p:Configuration=Debug /p:Platform=x64 /p:AppxBundle=Never, exit 0) and full test suite (run-tests.ps1) both re-run before and after the change: before, 138 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped; after, 143 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (138 prior + 5 new, all green, no prior test's behavior changed). A line-by-line diff review (git diff) confirms PrimaryWidget's three wrapper methods produce byte-identical StatusText/SetHeaderButtonsEnabled side effects and return values to the pre-fix version - no network call, UI side effect, or return value changed anywhere.

implementation_review.reason: LibraryOperationGuard.cs is a plain, dependency-free class picked up by the test project's Services\**\*.cs glob, its tests assert real mutual-exclusion behavior (TryBegin fails and IsRunning stays true when already running), PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs no longer contains the isLibraryOperationRunning field, and the diff preserves StatusText/SetHeaderButtonsEnabled ordering exactly with no new Seam introduced.
